stories.title: Employment related securities bulletin 68 (August 2026)
stories.summary: HMRC published its latest employment related securities bulletin covering changes to Enterprise Management Incentives notification requirements announced at Budget 2025.

stories.title: Tax news in brief — 5 August 2026
stories.summary: HMRC published Revenue & Customs Brief 7 (2026), explaining changes to the VAT capital goods scheme (CGS) effective from 29 July 2026.

stories.title: Property rental income statistics: 2026
stories.summary: HMRC announced an upcoming release of statistics on rental income and expenses declared by taxpayers via Income Tax Self-Assessment (ITSA) returns.

stories.title: Knife crime homicides fall to 30-year low
stories.summary: The Home Office reported that knife crime homicides have fallen to their lowest level in 30 years, alongside plans to overhaul officer disclosure rules.

stories.title: Dover crossings: 'One in, one out' deal returns 4% of migrants
stories.summary: New figures show the UK-France 'one in, one out' migrant returns deal has so far returned only 4% of small boat arrivals, prompting scrutiny of enhanced surveillance measures.

stories.title: Home Office blocking evacuation of women and children from Gaza
stories.summary: The Guardian reports the Home Office is blocking the evacuation of dozens of women and children from Gaza, drawing criticism from campaigners.

stories.title: DWP August payment dates change for Universal Credit and pensions
stories.summary: DWP confirmed that payments normally due on Friday 28 August will be paid early because 31 August is a bank holiday, affecting Universal Credit and State Pension recipients.

stories.title: Angela Eagle appointed Defra Secretary in Burnham's first Cabinet
stories.summary: Angela Eagle has been appointed Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs as part of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's newly formed Cabinet.

stories.title: Waste industry welcomes reports of Emma Hardy's appointment
stories.summary: The waste industry welcomed the appointment of Emma Hardy as the new minister for the circular economy and waste crime brief within Defra.

stories.title: 'Robot revolution': Government announces £20m funding for farming automation
stories.summary: The government announced up to £20m in funding to support technologies and robots that help farmers boost productivity, amid record-dry conditions this summer.

stories.title: NSI Act annual report 2025-26: another increase in deals reviewed
stories.summary: The National Security and Investment Act annual report shows another year-on-year increase in the number of transactions notified and reviewed for UK national security risk.

stories.title: Dame Chi Onwurah questions the sense in closing DSIT
stories.summary: A senior Labour MP has publicly questioned the government's decision to scrap DSIT and split its functions across three other departments, warning of fragmented tech policy.

stories.title: DSIT scrapped as Burnham government reshapes Whitehall tech functions
stories.summary: As part of PM Andy Burnham's Whitehall reshuffle, the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology is being abolished and its responsibilities redistributed.

stories.title: The best way to protect NHS patients' data
stories.summary: The Guardian examines proposals and debate around how to best safeguard NHS patient data amid ongoing digital reforms.

stories.title: Apple challenges UK government over data access request
stories.summary: Apple is challenging a UK government request for access to encrypted data, a dispute with implications for NHS and other public data security policy.

stories.title: More GP appointments in Nottingham and Nottinghamshire after surgery upgrades
stories.summary: A record 8.25 million GP appointments were provided across 126 Nottingham and Nottinghamshire practices in 2025/26, the highest number ever recorded, following surgery upgrades.

stories.title: Royal Mail proposes scrapping daily second-class post delivery
stories.summary: Royal Mail has proposed moving second-class post delivery to three days a week rather than daily, citing collapsing letter volumes as people move to digital communication.

stories.title: Royal Mail service update — 4 August 2026
stories.summary: Royal Mail issued a service update on its air and road network moving letters and parcels between distribution hubs and delivery offices.

stories.title: Royal Mail delivery targets: four-digit code you don't want to see
stories.summary: Royal Mail is now aiming to deliver 90% of first-class letters next day (down from 93%) and 95% of second-class mail within three days (down from previous targets).
